solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top Irish comic, one disregarded in Times

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the two Ts, as if held within them

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time; plural Times gives two of them, TT

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the remaining letters of Irish are played about with
one of the letters is ignored, so it drops out of the word Irish

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A comedian from Ireland heads the bill, though one is passed over in a newspaper review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one disregarded' removes an I from IRISH, leaving RISH; 'comic' rearranges that to SHIR, which goes 'in' TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a casual garment for the upper body, which clothing sellers call a top.

clue.text: Examine underground laboratory item

parts.note: to examine something is to test it
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Inspect an item of kit kept in a subterranean lab.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is the glass vessel for holding samples that every chemistry lab uses.

clue.text: Head office gripe about the foreign mortgage

indicators.note: the complaint word goes around the foreign article, enclosing it

parts.note: to gripe is to moan
EL is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Headquarters complains about the overseas mortgage arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan is money borrowed from a lender to buy a house, secured on that property.

clue.text: Go off to curb current uproar

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain, so the decay word holds the current symbol in check inside it

parts.note: food that goes off rots
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An explosion is meant to restrain the present commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public disturbance, a scene of tumult and noisy disorder.

clue.text: This writer's following gold fraud

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: this writer is = I'M
post means after, as in post-war
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A columnist admits his followers are drawn by a get-rich-quick scam.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be somebody else in order to deceive, which makes them a sham or cheat.

clue.text: Discombobulated tailor had deluded me

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and refashion, so these letters are made over into a new shape

explanation.surface: A confused customer says the tailor fooled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor' looks like the person doing the deceiving, but it is a verb telling you to rework the letters of HAD DELUDED ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddle-headed describes someone thinking unclearly, bewildered and confused, just as discombobulated does.

clue.text: Western sign in bar initially changed

indicators.note: the opening letter of the musical sign is swapped for another, its first letter altered

parts.note: an accidental is the sharp, flat or natural sign written within a bar of music

explanation.surface: A notice in a pub was altered at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' pretends to be a pub; it is a bar of music. ACCIDENTAL has its first letter A changed to O.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental comes from the Latin for the setting sun and refers to the West, opposite of oriental.

clue.text: Needlework that husband avoids as well

indicators.note: the word that avoids the husband, so his letter is left out of it

parts.note: as well means too

explanation.surface: A wife's sewing hobby is something her husband stays well clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a design pricked into the skin with a needle, so it is literally work done by needle.

clue.text: Flush communist lair

parts.note: a red is a communist
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Drive a Marxist out of his hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush is to go pink in the face, which is to turn red or redden.

clue.text: In order to appear in Paris we turned over millions

indicators.note: the millions are set in the middle of the turned-round French word
turned over means the French word is read backwards

parts.note: nous is French for we, as spoken in Paris
M stands for million; millions doubles it to MM

explanation.surface: To be noticed in the French capital, we gave away a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'order to appear'; the containment signal 'In' stands at the very start, before the pieces it governs, which disguises it as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone is to command them to come, as a court summons a witness.

clue.text: Learned banker's about to collect old coin

indicators.note: the river collects the coin, holding it within its letters
about here means turned round, so the river is read backwards

parts.note: a banker is cryptic for a river (it has banks); the Dee is a river in Britain
a ducat was a gold coin used in old Europe

explanation.surface: A learned financier is about to gather an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river, the Dee, not a financier; 'about' turns DEE to EED, which collects DUCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned and educated both describe someone who has acquired much knowledge through study.

clue.text: Supporters in gym imitate hurdles

parts.note: to parallel something is to match or mirror it
hurdles and bars are both obstacles

explanation.surface: Fitness fans copy each other and jump over obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel bars are a pair of raised rails in a gymnastics hall that hold the gymnast up.

clue.text: Brief legendary bowman

definitions.meaning: to brief someone is to ... them what they need to know
William ..., the Swiss archer of legend who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.surface: A short note on a mythical archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tell means inform, as briefing does; William Tell is the famous archer from Swiss folklore.

clue.text: Courses brought forward by angry European

parts.note: to table a proposal is to bring it forward for discussion
hot under the collar means angry

explanation.surface: Classes were proposed by an irate continental.
explanation.definitionFit: Table d'hôte is a fixed-price menu of several set dishes served as successive meal stages.

clue.text: Downgrade foreign articles on merit

parts.note: un is French for a, and der is German for the, so the phrase gives two articles together
merit and value are synonyms

explanation.surface: Reduce the worth of imported goods on their quality.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two articles from two languages, French and German. 'on' places them above VALUE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To undervalue something is to rate it below its worth, so in effect to downgrade it.

clue.text: Supporter in laundry radically changing mind

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
laundry is the washing

explanation.surface: An undergarment caught in the wash is utterly transformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainwashing is forcing someone to abandon their beliefs, transforming how they think.

clue.text: Honour firm stable worker expert sent round

indicators.note: the expert goes round the other pieces, wrapping them

parts.note: an ace is an expert
CO is short for company, a firm
a lad is a stable hand who looks after racehorses

explanation.surface: A company groom receives an award after the top rider sends him round.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, a mark of distinction given to someone.

clue.text: Tick off brother endlessly interrupting a course

indicators.note: the shortened brother breaks into the meal phrase, sitting inside it

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a monk is a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: Scold a friar who keeps butting in during a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: MONK loses its end to give MON, which goes into A DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to reprimand, which is the same as the informal British tick off.

clue.text: Sound like Blondin?

definitions.meaning: sound means sensible and stable, of good judgement
Charles Blondin was the tightrope walker who crossed Niagara Falls, so he had to keep his balance perfectly

explanation.surface: A noise resembling a famous acrobat.
explanation.walkthrough: Blondin was a 19th-century French tightrope walker; the question mark flags the playful literal sense of balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-balanced person is sane and sensible; a tightrope walker must literally be steady on the rope.

clue.text: Sorcerer's bogus article

parts.note: bogus means sham, fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The magician's goods are fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a priest or healer believed to command spirits, a kind of magician.

clue.text: Get tired running for pitcher

parts.note: to flag is to grow weary
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A baseball thrower starts to tire while running.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large jug for serving wine or ale, which is what a pitcher is too.

clue.text: Maybe drop Harry on fine very old bay, heading west

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as with Prince Hal
F stands for fine on pencil grades

indicators.note: in an across entry heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: a hound bays, or yells

explanation.surface: Perhaps Harry dropped a ship on a calm day in an old bay as he steered west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' is not water but a howl, YELL; 'heading west' turns it to LLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-volley is a stroke played just after the ball bounces; a drop shot or drop kick is a related example.

clue.text: African state unduly limits gallons for taking away

indicators.note: the word for unduly limits, or encloses, the gallons

parts.note: too means excessively, unduly

explanation.surface: A nation in Africa sets excessive restrictions on fuel sold to carry away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for taking away' is a second, cryptic definition: food bought to take away is 'to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a small West African country on the Gulf of Guinea between Ghana and Benin.

clue.text: Conservative politician tours area affected

indicators.note: the politician pieces travel around the area, enclosing it

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Tory MP visits a region hit by a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes behaviour that is deliberately exaggerated and theatrical, which is affected in the sense of put on.

clue.text: Old sailor everyone, say, backed in crew

indicators.note: the turned-round pieces are placed inside the crew word

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the pieces read right to left

parts.note: all means everyone
e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: An ancient mariner says everyone in his crew backed him.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL + EG 'backed' gives GELLA, set 'in' MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan was the 16th-century Portuguese explorer whose expedition first circled the globe.

clue.text: A female wears long dress for trip to watch big game

indicators.note: the woman is inside the garment, so the dress goes around her

parts.note: a sari is a long draped Indian garment

explanation.surface: A woman puts on a flowing gown for an outing to a major match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big game' suggests a sports final; here it means large wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, often in Africa, to observe or hunt large wild animals.

clue.text: No Poles seen working for cobblers

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: No Polish people have been seen employed as shoemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cobblers' is British slang for rubbish, not shoe menders. 'working' rearranges SEEN to ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, cobblers means rubbish or drivel, from rhyming slang cobblers' awls.

clue.text: Address waste water in small church

indicators.note: the urine word goes inside the two short abbreviations

parts.note: pee is bodily waste water, urine

explanation.surface: A sermon on sewage delivered in a little chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk given to an audience, which is what a speech is.
